Bench: J. Uma Devi
 The Honourable Sri Justice M. Seetharama Murti
 And
 The Honourable Ms. Justice J.Uma Devi
 Writ Petition No.43787 of 2018
Order:

(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice M.Seetharama Murti) This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed seeking verbatim the following relief:
"... declaring the action of the respondents Sales Tax Authority attending to the petitioner business premises trying to take samples of the tobacco products lying in the petitioner shop, further more harassing the petitioner one way or another that they are going to take action including coercive steps under the Food Safety Standard Act all are illegal, in violation of the law includes exceeds the jurisdiction, powers and authority even though they are no right to take such action or harassment under the Food Safety Standard Act against the petitioner trade except law laid down under the GST includes violation of Article 14 and 19 of the Constitution of India against the Rulings of Apex Court as well as other High Courts including issuance of notice,
dated 27.11.2018 by the 4th respondent, consequently by suspending the notice dated 27.11.2018 issued by the 4th respondent in the interest of justice and to such other order or orders as may be deemed fit and proper in the circumstances of the case."
2.
We have heard the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner and of learned Standing Counsel for Commercial Taxes appearing for the respondents and we have perused the material record.
3. Assailing the notice, dated 27.11.2018, issued by 4th respondent, the petitioner earlier filed W.P.No.41702 of 2018.
In the said writ petition, while adverting to and extracting the contents of the said notice, which is also impugned in the present writ petition, this Court granted an interim order, on 20.11.2018.

In the said interim order, this Court clearly observed that the impugned notice shows that 4th respondent has exceeded his brief and is attempting to invoke the provisions of the Food Safety Regulations, for which he is not a competent authority and, therefore, it is a clear case of abuse of power.
After granting an interim order, the stock of the petitioner was released and the said writ petition was disposed of by a final order.

Thereafter, according to the petitioner further M/S. Karunamaya Cigarette And Tobacco ... vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 25 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72676886/
1 harassment is being caused pursuant to the notice impugned, and, hence the present writ petition is filed.
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Standing Counsel having drawn the attention of this Court to the counter and also G.O.Ms.No.6, dated 09.01.2013, filed along with the counter, submitted that the 4th respondent, as per the terms of the said GO, is entitled to check the banned items and inform the enforcement authorities of Food Safety for taking necessary action and that the 4th respondent acted in accord with the terms of the said Government Order and that he did not exceed his jurisdiction.

He further submitted that in view of the interim order granted in the earlier writ petition and the disposal of the said writ petition subsequently, no order as sought for by the petitioner need be granted in this writ petition as no further action was at all taken and as no further action is under contemplation.
He further submitted that the allegations that the petitioner is being harassed etcetera are all false and invented.
5. Recording the submissions, the writ petition is disposed of directing the 4th respondent not to take any further action exceeding his jurisdiction pursuant to the impugned notice.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.

Gk THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE M. SEETHARAMA MURTI AND THE HONOURABLE MS.
JUSTICE J.UMA DEVI WRIT PETITION No.43787 of 2018 (Per the Hon'ble Sri Justice M.Seetharama Murti) 25th July, 2019.
